The best candidate is **C2**, the 0.573 pF capacitor at the non-inverting node `b`. In a unity-gain Sallen-Key section, shrinking C2 raises both the natural frequency and Q, which matches the high fc (1.26 MHz vs. ~0.94 MHz target) and high peaking (8.9 dB vs. 3.7 dB). The lower-than-expected attenuation at 10·fc also fits a higher cutoff. I did not run a simulation, so this ranking is based on hand analysis of the sensitivities, and the other two candidates are less certain.
